question: what is this company worth, and what does the price already assume?

In enterprise terms the bear case is worth {valuation.scenarios.bear.enterprise_value}, the base {valuation.scenarios.base.enterprise_value} and the bull {valuation.scenarios.bull.enterprise_value}; after net debt of {valuation.scenarios.base.net_debt} and operating lease liabilities of {valuation.scenarios.base.operating_lease_liability}, equity value is {valuation.scenarios.bear.equity_value}, {valuation.scenarios.base.equity_value} and {valuation.scenarios.bull.equity_value}, spread over diluted shares of {valuation.scenarios.base.diluted_shares}. The base case is my best reading rather than the midpoint of the other two. It takes year-one revenue growth of {valuation.scenarios.base.drivers.revenue_growth_year_one|pct}, below the trailing four-quarter growth of {ratios.growth.revenue.trailing_four_quarters|pct} because the raised full-year guide already implies deceleration against a rising base, but well above the three-year compound rate of {earnings_versus_cash.history.revenue_growth_three_year_compound|pct}; a GAAP operating margin that starts at {valuation.scenarios.base.drivers.operating_margin_year_one|pct}, above every fiscal year in the filed record and near where the second quarter's operating income of {ratios.growth.operating_income.this_quarter} on revenue of {ratios.growth.revenue.this_quarter} already ran, and drifts to {valuation.scenarios.base.drivers.operating_margin_year_ten|pct}, just under the fiscal 2020 and fiscal 2021 margins of {earnings_versus_cash.history.years.5.operating_margin|pct} and {earnings_versus_cash.history.years.4.operating_margin|pct}; reinvestment falling from {valuation.scenarios.base.drivers.reinvestment_rate_year_one|pct} to {valuation.scenarios.base.drivers.reinvestment_rate_year_ten|pct} of after-tax operating income as the working-capital release the accounting analyst calls a timing effect reverses; and terminal growth of {valuation.scenarios.base.drivers.terminal_growth|pct}, under the risk-free cap of {valuation.risk_free_rate_cap_on_terminal_growth|pct}. Every scenario is discounted at a WACC of {valuation.wacc|pct} and taxed at the filed effective rate of {valuation.tax_rate|pct}. The discount rate is high enough that the present value of the base terminal value, {valuation.scenarios.base.terminal_value_present}, is smaller than the present value of the ten explicit years, {valuation.scenarios.base.explicit_present}; cash flows beyond year ten carry less weight here than in a typical ten-year model. The bull case, which takes the guided adjusted operating margin as a permanent GAAP margin of {valuation.scenarios.bull.drivers.operating_margin_year_ten|pct}, grows year one at {valuation.scenarios.bull.drivers.revenue_growth_year_one|pct} and fades to terminal growth of {valuation.scenarios.bull.drivers.terminal_growth|pct}, is worth {valuation.scenarios.bull.value_per_share}; the bear case, in which one of the two named cloud customers defers and the margin returns to the middle of the company's own range at {valuation.scenarios.bear.drivers.operating_margin_year_ten|pct}, is worth {valuation.scenarios.bear.value_per_share}.

price_position.reading: The price at the cutoff, {valuation.price_at_cutoff}, sits {valuation.price_position}: above the bull value of {valuation.value_range_per_share.high}, and far above the base value of {valuation.scenarios.base.value_per_share} and the bear value of {valuation.value_range_per_share.low}. In aggregate, the market value of equity at that price is {cost_of_capital.market_value_of_equity.value}, against a bull-case equity value of {valuation.scenarios.bull.equity_value} and a base-case equity value of {valuation.scenarios.base.equity_value}. No scenario I could build from the filed record reaches the price, including one that treats the company's adjusted-margin guidance as a permanent GAAP margin and grows revenue in year one faster than any fiscal year in its history. Part of the distance is the discount rate: the WACC of {cost_of_capital.wacc.value|pct} rests on a beta of {cost_of_capital.beta.value} measured from {cost_of_capital.beta.window_first} to {cost_of_capital.beta.window_last}, which lifts the cost of equity to {cost_of_capital.cost_of_equity.value|pct}; the sensitivity grid shows that a lower rate raises value, but a one-point step lifts the base only to {valuation.sensitivity.grid.0.1.value_per_share}, nowhere near the price. The rest of the distance is growth and margin that the price assumes and the record does not yet show, which the reverse DCF makes explicit.

market_implied_growth.reading: Holding {valuation.reverse_dcf.held}, the constant annual revenue growth for ten years at which the base case is worth the price is {valuation.reverse_dcf.value|pct}. Against the company's own record that rate has no precedent. Three-year compound revenue growth is {earnings_versus_cash.history.revenue_growth_three_year_compound|pct}; the best fiscal year in the filed history, fiscal 2023, grew {earnings_versus_cash.history.years.2.revenue_growth|pct} and fiscal 2024 then fell {earnings_versus_cash.history.years.1.revenue_growth|pct}; the trailing four quarters, which contain the strongest stretch of the AI-driven cycle, grew {ratios.growth.revenue.trailing_four_quarters|pct}, and the latest quarter grew {ratios.growth.revenue.year_over_year|pct} year over year. The company's own raised guide for fiscal 2026, quoted below, states a full-year rate below the implied rate, and the third-quarter revenue guide in the same release sits only modestly above the second quarter's revenue of {ratios.growth.revenue.this_quarter}, so the year-on-year pace is already decelerating as the prior-year base rises. The implied rate also does not fade: my bull case starts at {valuation.scenarios.bull.drivers.revenue_growth_year_one|pct} and fades to {valuation.scenarios.bull.drivers.terminal_growth|pct} by year ten, whereas the reverse DCF needs the implied rate held flat through year ten. Two caveats on how to read it. The implied growth is computed on base margins running from {valuation.scenarios.base.drivers.operating_margin_year_one|pct} to {valuation.scenarios.base.drivers.operating_margin_year_ten|pct}; a reader who believes the guided adjusted margin becomes the GAAP margin would need less growth to reach the price, but my bull case does exactly that and still lands at {valuation.scenarios.bull.value_per_share}. And it is computed at the WACC of {valuation.wacc|pct}; a lower discount rate would lower the implied growth, and the grid gives the scale of that effect. What the price assumes, then, is some combination of a decade of growth above anything in the filed record, margins above the company's own adjusted guidance, and a discount rate well below the one its own measured beta produces.

most_sensitive.assumption: the revenue growth and operating margin path (the scenario drivers)
most_sensitive.reading: The scenario spread dwarfs the sensitivity grid. Moving year-one revenue growth from {valuation.scenarios.bear.drivers.revenue_growth_year_one|pct} to {valuation.scenarios.bull.drivers.revenue_growth_year_one|pct}, the year-ten operating margin from {valuation.scenarios.bear.drivers.operating_margin_year_ten|pct} to {valuation.scenarios.bull.drivers.operating_margin_year_ten|pct} and terminal growth from {valuation.scenarios.bear.drivers.terminal_growth|pct} to {valuation.scenarios.bull.drivers.terminal_growth|pct} takes value per share from {valuation.scenarios.bear.value_per_share} to {valuation.scenarios.bull.value_per_share}, around a base of {valuation.scenarios.base.value_per_share}. The two drivers compound through the terminal year: year-ten free cash flow to the firm is {valuation.scenarios.bear.years.9.free_cash_flow_to_firm} in the bear case, {valuation.scenarios.base.years.9.free_cash_flow_to_firm} in the base and {valuation.scenarios.bull.years.9.free_cash_flow_to_firm} in the bull, and the present value of the terminal value runs from {valuation.scenarios.bear.terminal_value_present} to {valuation.scenarios.bull.terminal_value_present}. Of the two, the margin path is the one the record argues about most. The second quarter's GAAP operating margin already sits near the base year-one level, but the three-year average is {earnings_versus_cash.history.operating_margin_three_year_average|pct} and the trailing figure {ratios.profitability.operating_margin|pct}, the filed history includes a year in which revenue fell, and the accounting analyst reads share-based compensation of {terms.trailing_four_quarters.share_based_compensation}, the Nubis holdback and the restructuring charge that recurs every period as real costs that the adjusted guide excludes. The growth path, in turn, rests on two cloud customers the release says together supplied about a third of quarterly revenue, on a backlog whose conversion language the filing loosened, and on purchase commitments of {terms.balances_now.unconditional_purchase_obligations} that must be honored by suppliers before the backlog can ship.

most_sensitive.assumption: the discount rate (WACC), which is beta-driven
most_sensitive.reading: On the grid, one point of WACC moves the base value from {valuation.sensitivity.grid.0.1.value_per_share} at a point lower to {valuation.sensitivity.grid.2.1.value_per_share} at a point higher, while half a point of terminal growth moves it only from {valuation.sensitivity.grid.1.0.value_per_share} to {valuation.sensitivity.grid.1.2.value_per_share}; the corners run from {valuation.sensitivity.grid.2.0.value_per_share} to {valuation.sensitivity.grid.0.2.value_per_share}. The discount rate therefore matters more than terminal growth, and the rate here is high. The WACC of {cost_of_capital.wacc.value|pct} is almost entirely the cost of equity of {cost_of_capital.cost_of_equity.value|pct}, since the equity weight is {cost_of_capital.weights.equity|pct}, and that cost of equity is the risk-free rate of {cost_of_capital.risk_free_rate.value|pct} plus a beta of {cost_of_capital.beta.value} times an equity risk premium of {cost_of_capital.equity_risk_premium.value|pct}. The beta is measured over the window {cost_of_capital.beta.window_first} to {cost_of_capital.beta.window_last}, a period in which the share moved far more than the market. A reader using a lower beta would discount at a lower rate and reach a higher value in every scenario, and the terminal value, which is a minority of enterprise value at this rate, would grow in weight; the grid's one-point step shows the direction and the scale, and shows that the price would remain well above the range. The cost of capital is not mine to choose, so the grid is the whole of what can be said about it here.

accounting_adjustments.reading: One adjustment was applied: '{valuation.accounting_adjustments.each.0.name}', carried from the accounting analysis as a one-time reduction to cash flow ({valuation.accounting_adjustments.each.0.mechanism}). It moved the base value per share by {valuation.accounting_adjustments.each.0.moved_per_share}, from {valuation.accounting_adjustments.base_value_per_share} to {valuation.accounting_adjustments.all_together.value_per_share}; all adjustments together move {valuation.accounting_adjustments.all_together.moved_per_share} per share. The amount is the year-over-year build in accounts payable of {earnings_versus_cash.working_capital.accounts_payable.balance_sheet_change}, which MD&A ties to the timing of payments to suppliers and the accounting analyst reads as a release that reverses, spread over diluted shares of {valuation.scenarios.base.diluted_shares}. It is small beside the scenario spread and beside the distance to the price. Items the accounting analyst flagged but could not size carry no adjustment: the new long-term unbilled software-licence receivable, the Nubis holdback labelled one-time, the restructuring charge excluded from adjusted results every period, and the Blue Planet goodwill left unchanged as that segment turned to losses. Two further things enter the valuation through the drivers rather than as adjustments. Share-based compensation of {terms.trailing_four_quarters.share_based_compensation} is inside the GAAP operating margins I chose, which is why the base margin sits below the adjusted guide. And the tax rate of {valuation.tax_rate|pct}, which the income-tax note attributes partly to share-based deductions and jurisdiction mix, is applied to every year's operating income in every scenario; a higher and more ordinary rate would lower every value in the range.

limits: This valuation is a set of stated assumptions run through a stated formula. It states no recommendation to trade, and a different reader choosing different drivers would reach a different value.
